sentences.text: A site that `create-cairn-site` scaffolded arrives as a complete SvelteKit project in a GitHub repository, already deployed as a Cloudflare Worker, with the engine, `@glw907/cairn-cms`, installed as one npm dependency.
Its tree is Waymark, cairn's reference reading theme, set on a chassis of design-neutral plumbing and copied from the same tree the engine tests itself against.

SvelteKit routes mount the admin and the public site, a server hook guards `/admin`, and the whole SvelteKit config sits inline in `vite.config.ts`, while `wrangler.jsonc` binds the Worker's one D1 database (the auth store), a mail binding, and an R2 bucket.
The repository holds the code and the markdown, the site's GitHub App commits each editor's publish into it, and a GitHub Actions workflow checks every push and pull request.
Every file in that tree belongs to the site.

The engine's npm package carries neither Waymark nor the chassis, so an engine upgrade moves the `@glw907/cairn-cms` range and leaves the tree as it is, and any edit a release needs in the site's code is the site's to make.
Ownership still leaves some files with readers that depend on them.
The engine reads the adapter, the server hook, and the bindings, and the admin commits editors' work into the content, its manifests, and the primary menu in the site config.
A few more feed the CI workflow and the build's prerender checks, and either one fails when such a file breaks its rule.
Those files share directories with files that only the site reads, as the adapter does with the theme's style sheets in `src/theme/`.
An owner who knows which files carry a contract can change the rest freely and change those few with the contract kept.
A developer who ran the setup command, or who took over a site from someone who did, reads on to learn what each file does and whether to change it.

One who took over also lacks what the command left outside the repository: its saved record of the run on the machine that ran it and, when the run connected Workers Builds, a build token whose revocation stops deploys without warning.

A reader who knows the engine's import points and seams from [Architecture](architecture.md) finds where each one lands in the tree, and a reader working on the public theme finds the files around it.
A developer still choosing between the setup command and a by-hand build sees what the command writes.
A developer adding cairn to an app that already exists has no choice to make, because the setup command writes only into a missing or empty directory.
The following subjects appear in this order:
What the scaffold is, and why the site owns every file
The file tree, with the files the engine or a check reads marked
The root files, the build and deploy configuration with the Worker's one D1 database, and the migrations, with why an added database takes a separate directory
The routes and the server hook, including what the local dev server runs
The theme, chassis, and content directories, the committed manifests, and the two style sheets
The settings a new owner edits by hand, outside the admin
The build's crawl rules and the themed 404 page
The state the setup command left outside the repository

The page assumes working knowledge of SvelteKit's project structure (routes, layouts, hooks, and prerendering), Vite configuration, and Wrangler configuration for a Worker's bindings and D1 migrations.
It explains no SvelteKit or Cloudflare basics.
Other pages cover the following related subjects:
Building the same tree by hand: [Add cairn to a SvelteKit app](add-cairn-to-a-sveltekit-app.md)
Changing the theme and the chassis: [Theme your public site](theme-your-public-site.md)
Building a custom admin screen: [Add a custom admin screen](add-a-custom-admin-screen.md)
Each delivery route's wiring: [Build the public routes](build-the-public-routes.md)
Media configuration behind the `MEDIA_BUCKET` binding: [Configure media](configure-media.md)
The audit's `cairn-audit.config.json` in depth: [Run cairn-audit on your site](run-cairn-audit-on-your-site.md)
A scaffolded site is Waymark, cairn's reference theme, wired onto a chassis of design-neutral plumbing, and the setup command copies both from the same tree the engine runs its tests against.
That tree is `examples/showcase`, and the copy leaves out the following groups:
The Playwright suite and the test routes
The design-review tooling, the `theme-kit` and `probe-craft` routes
The members-login fixture: `src/members`, `src/routes/members`, and `migrations-members/`
The `admin/signups` example screen and its `migrations-app/` database
The `admin/error-fixture` route
The `env-check.ts` module in `src/lib/` and the file `src/routes/(site)/+layout.server.ts`
The showcase's `scripts/`, `README.md`, `.claude`, `.cairn`, and `cairn-audit.config.json`
The 13 posts dated 2025, out of the showcase's 27, so the scaffold keeps the other 14
The template build writes a fresh `README.md`, `scripts/dev.mjs`, `.claude` guidance, and `cairn-audit.config.json` in place of the showcase's, so the scaffold still carries those files.
Waymark is the only template the setup command ships.
A second template, Topo, is planned but not shipped.
The same run that writes the tree creates the site's GitHub App and repository, provisions its Cloudflare bindings, and deploys it, so the tree arrives already live.
Every file in the tree belongs to the site: the engine's npm package carries neither the template nor the chassis, and the engine arrives as one ordinary dependency in `package.json`.
A site built by hand starts with neither.
[Add cairn to a SvelteKit app](add-cairn-to-a-sveltekit-app.md) walks through that build.
Owning a file does not remove a contract on it, and a file that the engine or a check reads can still break the build, the deploy, or the admin when it changes.
The file tree marks each file that carries such a contract.

In the tree the setup command writes, `[engine]` marks a file the engine reads, writes, or requires a shape of, and `[gate]` marks a file that runs or feeds a check that can fail the build or the CI run.
The tree leaves out files no section discusses, such as `src/app.html` and the theme's test files.
The scaffold has no `src/access.ts`, no `.dev.vars.example`, and no `LICENSE`.
`CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/` hold Claude Code's guidance files; see [Using Claude Code with cairn](../claude-code/using-claude-code-with-cairn.md).

Beside a plain SvelteKit project's files, the root carries a CI workflow, the audit's config, and a `.gitignore` that the setup command renames, and local secrets go in a `.dev.vars` the owner creates there.
On every push and pull request, the workflow installs dependencies and runs `npm run check` and `npm run check:cairn`.
It uses Node 24.
Nothing else in the scaffold names a Node version: there is no `.nvmrc` and no `engines` field.
The last step runs `npx cairn-guidance check` without `--strict` and under `continue-on-error: true`, and that step never fails the job.
No browser is installed, so `check:cairn:rendered` cannot run in the workflow.
The scaffold ships no `.dev.vars.example`: local secrets go in a `.dev.vars` that the owner creates and the `.gitignore` keeps out of the repository.
Only the Deploy-button tree, `templates/waymark/`, carries a template for it.
That tree is a separate committed copy, built from the same template build plus an overlay.
In that tree, `.dev.vars.example` names the following two entries:
`GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_B64`, the GitHub App's private key, with a placeholder value.
The App id and installation id are not secrets and live in the adapter, so the file omits them.
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, left empty.
Tidy reads it only when tidy is enabled in `site.config.yaml`, and the scaffold's `site.config.yaml` ships with tidy enabled.
For more information, see [Turn on tidy](turn-on-tidy.md) and [Rotate the GitHub App key](rotate-the-github-app-key.md).
The audit's config names both compiled admin sheets, so the static audit sees every class that a site's admin route writes.
The two sheets are the engine's `node_modules/@glw907/cairn-cms/dist/admin/cairn-admin.css` and the site's `.cairn/admin.css`.
For the rest of the config, see [Run cairn-audit on your site](run-cairn-audit-on-your-site.md).
The setup command's package stores this file as `gitignore`, because npm's packlist drops a file named `.gitignore`, and the setup command renames it after copying.
The rename fails loudly when the file is absent, and `.gitattributes` ships with its name unchanged.
The file ignores `.dev.vars` and every `.dev.vars.*` file, with no line that re-includes any of them.
It also ignores the whole root `.cairn/` directory (`/.cairn/`).
The pre-scripts rebuild the compiled `.cairn/admin.css` there.
The remaining root entries are a plain project's files, plus a generated types file and the directory that holds the dev server's launcher.
The plain files are `README.md`, `.prettierignore`, `.prettierrc`, `tsconfig.json`, and `vitest.config.ts`, and the root has no `LICENSE`.
`worker-configuration.d.ts` is generated `wrangler types` output, and `src/app.d.ts` references it.
The `dev` script runs `scripts/dev.mjs`.
`package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, and `wrangler.jsonc` configure how the site builds and deploys, and `src/app.d.ts` types what they provide.
`npm run build` runs `vite build`, and the build produces the Worker that `wrangler.jsonc` names as `main`.
The engine, `@glw907/cairn-cms`, sits in `dependencies`, and the `imports` field declares `#chassis`, `#theme`, and `#lib` as subpath imports rather than config aliases.
[Upgrade cairn](upgrade-cairn.md) covers moving the engine's range.
The field maps `#lib/*` to `./src/lib/*`.
That directory holds one file.
`log.ts` is the site's [`createLogger`](../reference/log.md#createlogger) instance, typed over the site's log event names.
The following table describes what the scaffold's main scripts run.
Script
What it runs
`dev`
It compiles the admin sheet, then runs `scripts/dev.mjs`, which starts `vite dev` with `CAIRN_DEV_BACKEND=1` beside a Tailwind watch compile.
The local admin runs on the in-memory dev backend.
`build`
It runs `vite build` after the same compile.
`predev`, `prebuild`, `precheck`
Each compiles `src/admin.css` into `.cairn/admin.css`, so a Workers Builds build needs no separate admin-stylesheet step.
`check:cairn`
It compiles the admin sheet, then runs `cairn-audit`, which fails only on an unsuppressed error-tier finding.
Public-scope findings print as advisories.
A missing `daisyui` or `tailwindcss` peer fails the run with a message that names the peer.
`check:cairn:rendered`
It runs `cairn-audit --rendered`, which needs a real browser against a running admin.
The scaffold ships no Playwright dependency, so the script does not run as shipped.
`cairn:manifest`
It runs `cairn-manifest`.
`format`, `format:check`
They run Prettier.
`test:unit`
It runs `vitest run`.
`cf-typegen`
It runs `wrangler types --include-runtime=false`, the arguments the committed `worker-configuration.d.ts` records.
Only the Deploy-button tree's script adds `--env-file=.dev.vars.example`.
The scaffold carries no `svelte.config.js`, so the whole SvelteKit config passes inline to `sveltekit()` in this file.
That config sets the Cloudflare adapter and a prerender `handleHttpError` that throws on every HTTP error during prerendering.
[Crawl rules](#crawl-rules) explains what the build needs to keep passing.
The config sets no `csrf` key, so SvelteKit's Origin check runs ahead of every handle, `/admin` included, and cairn's double-submit token sits on top of it.
SvelteKit 3 removed `csrf.checkOrigin`, and a config that sets it fails validation.
For more information, see [CSRF protection](security-model.md#csrf-protection).
The `cairnManifest` plugin verifies the committed content manifest on build.
Its `config` hook defines `__CAIRN_DEV_BUILD__` for the dev backend to gate on, and the scaffold's config sets no define.
The config also lists `@glw907/cairn-cms-dev` in `ssr.noExternal`.
That package ships built JavaScript that imports `cloudflare:workers`, a module Node's loader rejects, and without the entry `/admin` answers 500 under `vite dev`.
The Worker's config declares four bindings, the static-assets binding `ASSETS` among them, and one variable, and its only D1 database is the auth store.
The following list names each one:
`ASSETS`, the static-assets binding, on the `assets` block
`AUTH_DB`, the D1 database that holds the auth store
`EMAIL`, the Email Sending binding
`MEDIA_BUCKET`, the R2 bucket
`PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, a variable
The scaffold binds no second database.
[Configure media](configure-media.md) covers the media settings behind the bucket.
The config sets `observability.enabled` to `true`.
[Workers Logs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/logs/workers-logs/) records a Worker's logs only with that setting on.
The config also sets `assets.not_found_handling` to `"none"`, and [Themed 404 page](#themed-404-page) explains why.

This file imports `@glw907/cairn-cms/ambient`, which declares the `__CAIRN_DEV_BUILD__` global, and it types `App.PageData` with the optional `nav`, `footerNav`, `siteName`, and `hasIslands` fields that the root layout load returns.
It references `@cloudflare/workers-types` and `worker-configuration.d.ts`, whose `Env` types the Worker bindings that `cloudflare:workers` exposes.
For more information, see [Ambient types](../reference/ambient.md).
The `migrations/` directory holds the auth store's schema for `AUTH_DB`, and it is the scaffold's only migrations directory.
It carries `0000_auth.sql`, `0001_roles.sql`, `0003_preview.sql`, and `0004_login_nonce.sql`.
The opt-in `0002_audit.sql` is absent, because only a site that wires `createD1AuditSink` applies it.
[Wire the audit sink](add-a-custom-admin-screen.md#wire-the-audit-sink) covers adding it.
`0001_roles.sql` is needed once a site declares roles beyond the default owner and editor pair, and the scaffold ships it, so a new site already has it.
Any automated `wrangler d1 migrations apply` runs it.
Its rebuild keeps only the engine's four `editor` columns, so a site carries any columns it added across first.
`0003_preview.sql` serves draft-preview links.
A database the site adds takes a separate migrations directory.
`wrangler d1 migrations apply` walks one directory per database, and a directory shared with `migrations/` would apply each schema to both databases.
The server hook installs the auth guard over `/admin`, and the routes split into that admin mount, a prerendered public site in the `(site)` group, and endpoints at the root.
The following tree shows `src/params.ts` and the route directories and root files under `src/routes/`.
The hook picks `devBackendHandle` or `createAuthGuard` in one `if` and exports the result as `handle`.
The test reads the build-time `__CAIRN_DEV_BUILD__` define first, then the runtime opt-in `CAIRN_DEV_BACKEND === '1'`.
The opt-in reads the Worker env and falls back to `process.env`, because `vite dev` runs the hooks in Node, where the platform proxy's env never carries the shell variable that `npm run dev` sets.
Both handles take the composed `runtime` from `#chassis/cairn.server.js`.
The guard gates the whole `/admin` subtree before any load runs.
Per-route authorization belongs to `requireAccess` and `createSectionAction`.
The [`createAuthGuard`](../reference/sveltekit.md#createauthguard) entry documents the guard's config.
The scaffold's adapter declares no `access` member and takes the zero-config owner and editor floor, and the tree holds no `src/access.ts`.
[Restrict admin access](restrict-admin-access.md) covers declaring an access map.
On the dev branch, `devBackendHandle` installs in-memory stand-ins for the GitHub backend, the media bucket, and `AUTH_DB`, and it signs in an owner with no email.
Its state lasts as long as the server process, and nothing leaves the machine.
The hook passes no `content` option, so the dev admin lists the site's entries from its working tree.
That default is the `'repository'` mode, and the `'fixtures'` mode seeds an in-memory repository with sample content instead.
In `'repository'` mode, edits land in an in-memory overlay over the working tree.
Nothing is written to disk, and the overlay lasts until the dev server restarts.
The admin mount is one catch-all pair, `[...path]/+page.server.ts` and `+page.svelte`, beside the shared layout pair, `+layout.server.ts` and `+layout.svelte`.
The [canonical admin mount](../reference/admin-routes.md#the-route-files-plus-the-composer) reference reproduces both pairs.
The directory also holds `+error.svelte`.
It renders an error inside `/admin` within the admin shell.
A 403 and a 404 each show a message and a **Back to the dashboard** link to `/admin`, and any other status shows the thrown message.
A failure in the admin layout's load still falls to the root error page.
[Add a custom admin screen](add-a-custom-admin-screen.md) covers adding a screen under this mount.
The entry catch-all `[...path]` and its raw-markdown twin `[...path=md]` coexist through `createPublicRoutes`, and `src/params.ts` defines the `md` matcher.
That file uses SvelteKit's `defineParams`.
The group also holds the `preview/[token]/` route.
The `archive/[page]` route slices its page with the chassis `archive.ts` helper.
The `styleguide/` route renders every registered markdown component, with a sample for each one that declares a `preview`, plus the type scale and the component recipes.
[Build the public routes](build-the-public-routes.md) covers each route's wiring.
The root holds the feed, sitemap, and robots endpoints beside two routes that sit outside `/admin` on purpose, the media route and `/healthz`.
The feed and sitemap endpoints are `feed.json/`, `feed.xml/`, and `sitemap.xml/`.
The `robots.txt/` route reads a `posture` option that sets its stance toward AI training crawlers.
[Choose an AI posture](choose-an-ai-posture.md) covers the choice.
The `media/[...path]/` route exports the [`createMediaRoute`](../reference/sveltekit.md#createmediaroute) handler.
It validates each request and streams the object from `MEDIA_BUCKET`, adding security headers because the route sits outside `/admin`.
The `/healthz` route sits outside the guard.
It answers with the payload that [`loadHealth`](../reference/sveltekit.md#loadhealth) returns, as JSON with status 200 when `ok` is true and 503 when it is false.
A thrown error becomes a 503 with the fixed detail `health check failed`.
Every answer carries `cache-control: no-store`, and the route exports `prerender = false`.
The root `+layout.server.ts` returns the menus, the site name, and whether the site registers any island, and it reads them without importing the full adapter.
The load returns `nav`, `footerNav`, `siteName`, and `hasIslands`, and it reads `site-config.ts` and the island registry to keep each request that is not prerendered light.
`SiteHeader` and the root `+error.svelte` read those values through `page.data`.
The root `+error.svelte` is the themed 404 and error page.
`src/theme/` holds the adapter and Waymark's design, the chassis holds the plumbing every scaffolded site shares, and `src/content/` holds the markdown and its committed manifests.
The adapter shares `src/theme/` with the theme's style sheets, so a file's directory does not show whether it carries a contract.
The adapter, `cairn.config.ts`, is one `defineAdapter` call over `content`, `backend`, `email`, `media`, `rendering`, and an `editor` group carrying `nav`, `navLayout`, and `preview`.
The site imports it as `#theme/cairn.config.js`, and the `cairnManifest` `configModule` in `vite.config.ts` names it.
In `navLayout`, the `Site` group carries only engine screens (`vocabulary`, `nav`, `settings`, and `editors`), and the `Content` group carries the `media` entry.

For more information, see [Define an adapter and schema](define-an-adapter-and-schema.md), [Arrange the admin sidebar](arrange-the-admin-sidebar.md), and [Customize the sign-in email](add-cairn-to-a-sveltekit-app.md#customize-the-sign-in-email).
Besides the adapter, the directory holds the following files:
`site-config.ts`: the one `parseSiteConfig` call site, over `site.config.yaml`
`site.config.yaml`: the site name, the description, the primary and footer menus, the tag `vocabulary`, `spellcheck` with its `dialect`, and `tidy`, shipped enabled
`markdown-components.ts`: nine `defineComponent` declarations, one of them hydrated
`icons.ts`: the `IconSet` that the components and the icon picker draw from
`components/`: `ArticleView.svelte`, `EntryRow.svelte`, `SiteFooter.svelte`, `SiteHeader.svelte`, and `admin-link.ts`
`islands/`: `Banner.svelte`, `banner-expiry.ts`, and a `registry.ts` that maps `banner` to `Banner.svelte`
`theme.css` and `site.css`: the theme's tokens and page styling
`theme-names.ts`: the daisyUI theme names, which `src/app.html` and `theme.css` repeat
[Theme your public site](theme-your-public-site.md) covers changing the design.
The chassis is the design-neutral plumbing every scaffolded site shares, copied into the tree with Waymark.
The engine's package carries none of it, so the chassis belongs to the site like every other file.
[Port your theme onto the chassis](theme-your-public-site.md#port-your-theme-onto-the-chassis) describes where the chassis ends and the theme begins.
The chassis also holds the archive's page size, described in [Settings outside the admin](#settings-outside-the-admin).
Content is markdown with YAML frontmatter, one directory per concept, named by the concept's `dir`.
The scaffold declares `posts`, `pages`, and `fragments`, seeded with 14 sample posts, two pages, and one fragment.
Because the adapter names each directory, renaming one is an adapter change.
This directory holds three committed files that the engine and its build tools write.
Each file has a different writer:
`index.json`: the content manifest.
The `cairnManifest` plugin and `cairn-manifest` regenerate it and fail the build when it drifts from the markdown, and each publish commit patches it.
`media.json`: the media registry, written by the admin's media upload, metadata, and delete commits.
`site-facts.json`: a file that `cairn-manifest` writes.
The `cairn:manifest` script runs `cairn-manifest`.
For more information, see the [`cairnManifest`](../reference/vite.md#cairnmanifest) reference and [The `site-facts.json` contract](../reference/site-facts.md).
The site compiles two separate sets of styles, the admin's from `src/admin.css` and the public site's from `theme.css` and `site.css`.
`src/admin.css` ends with an import of `@glw907/cairn-cms/admin-sources.css`.
That engine file holds only the `@source` directives for the engine's shipped admin markup.
The pre-scripts compile `src/admin.css` into `.cairn/admin.css`, inside the gitignored root `.cairn/` directory.
The audit config still names the engine's precompiled `dist` sheet, and the import does not replace it.
The compiled `.cairn/admin.css` is the other sheet the config names, and [`cairn-audit.config.json`](#cairn-auditconfigjson) lists both.
`theme.css` and `site.css` hold the theme's tokens and page styling.
Beneath them sit two lower layers: the engine's `cairn-public.css` roles, which the chassis `tokens.css` imports right after Tailwind, and the chassis's design-scale defaults.
[Re-skin Waymark](theme-your-public-site.md#re-skin-waymark) covers how the layers combine.
The archive's page size and the footer menu are set in files, outside the admin.
`ARCHIVE_PAGE_SIZE` in `src/chassis/archive.ts` is the one page-size setting for both the home page and the archive, and the scaffold sets it to 13.
Both paginate every post after the newest one, and the home page shows that one as its lead.
The page `/archive/2` therefore first exists once more than 14 posts are published.
`/admin/nav` edits only the primary menu.
The footer menu is a flat menu that the developer edits by hand in `site.config.yaml`.
The prerender crawl fails the build on an unseen route or an HTTP error, and the scaffold keeps its build passing with one route exemption and one link attribute.
`handleUnseenRoutes` exempts only `/(site)/archive/[page]`.
A corpus that fits on page one gives that route no entries, and SvelteKit's crawl-completeness check would otherwise fail the build.
Any other unseen prerenderable route still throws.
A link to `/admin` in prerendered public markup carries `rel="external"` so that the crawler never requests it.
Every `/admin` route answers a build-time crawl with an error, and `handleHttpError` throws on any HTTP error.
The header and footer apply the attribute through the shared `isAdminHref` predicate.
A new `/admin` link in public markup needs the same attribute.
For the prerender options, see SvelteKit's [Vite plugin reference](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/@sveltejs-kit-vite).
A scaffolded site serves a themed 404 page through two pieces that need each other, the root `src/routes/+error.svelte` and `assets.not_found_handling` set to `"none"` in `wrangler.jsonc`.
The prerendered `(site)` group's catch-all is stripped from the runtime manifest, so that group's layout never runs for an unmatched path.
The root `+error.svelte` therefore rebuilds the site chrome itself.
It reads the menus and the site name through `page.data` from the root `+layout.server.ts`.
On the Worker's side, `"none"` passes an unmatched request to the Worker.
The `"404-page"` setting would instead serve an unthemed static file from the edge without running the Worker.
Cloudflare's [Worker script routing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/routing/worker-script/) page documents the setting.

The setup command kept its record of the run on the machine that ran it, and when its Workers Builds chapter connected the repository, it registered the Cloudflare API token pasted during setup as the build token the site's deploys use.
The record sits at `~/.config/cairn/sites/<id>.json`, in a directory with mode 0700 and a file with mode 0600, and never under the project directory.
It includes the pasted Cloudflare token.
A `--yes` run reads the token from `CAIRN_CF_API_TOKEN` and refuses a token-shaped value on the command line.
A developer who took over the site from someone else has no copy of that record, because it sits in the home directory of whoever ran the command.
On a resumed run, `--org`, `--repo-name`, `--app-name`, and `--owner-email` override a saved answer for any chapter that has not yet run.
The `--brand-color` flag accepts a `#`-prefixed hex color, an `oklch(...)` string, or a bare number read as a hue in degrees, and any other shape fails.
The setup run's Workers Builds chapter either connects the repository or records a decline.
The `--connect` flag re-enters that chapter only for a site at or past its first deploy.
The chapter registers the pasted token as the build token named `cairn create-cairn-site build token`, reusing an existing build token that wraps the same token id.
Revoking or rolling that token at Cloudflare breaks automatic deploys with no prior warning.
The next commit still triggers a build, and the build fails.
